run.display_title: Reuse CI compiler caches and preserve qualified analysis execution (#80)

head_commit.message:
Reuse CI compiler caches and preserve qualified analysis execution (#80)

* Fix iOS source archive identity and publisher failure handling

Introduced by: The independent iOS source archive generation added in #64 relied on each runner's gzip default. Run 39035206621 exposed different defaults on the Intel and ARM producers.

Use case and reproduction: Continuous publication consumes both macOS packages and one shared iOS source set. The failed run's Intel and ARM source tar streams are identical, but recompressing at levels 9 and 6 reproduces their different archive hashes exactly. The publisher correctly rejects the Intel package's source-set binding. Existing cross-architecture tests mocked archive generation and missed this runtime difference.

Fix: Explicitly select gzip level 9 while preserving strict source receipt verification. Add a real-compression regression that models both host defaults. Authenticate the publishing PAT with a read-only request before downloads, and run failure/cancellation rollback only after candidate creation was attempted, including failed or cancelled creates without an emitted ID. Enforce these workflow contracts with fail-closed lint mutations and credential tests.

Verification: Passed all 75 iOS release-contract tests, 12 GitHub API helper tests, and 204 CI-quality lint tests. Focused coverage also passes Python 3.9. Regenerated legal assets from the failing run's actual source and native artifacts have identical receipts under both gzip defaults and Python 3.9/3.14; the native verifier accepts all eight x86_64 dylibs. Actionlint passes with only its existing concurrency.queue syntax limitation excluded, also reproduced on the unchanged base.

Operational follow-up: KLOGG_GITHUB_TOKEN returned HTTP 401 and must be replaced in repository Actions secrets. This change does not alter secrets or relax PAT permissions; fresh CI artifacts are required before publishing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Share analysis execution between qualification and ordinary CI

Use case: Qualify the same static-analysis and coverage policy that ordinary CI consumes, without maintaining a second workflow implementation.

Root cause: The qualification helper and consumer workflows separately owned configure options, generated headers, translation-unit selection, analyzer arguments, gcovr reports, and coverage ratcheting. Updating one path could leave the other behind.

How to fix: Expose shared phases through run_linux_analysis.sh and compose them in both callers. Keep event resolution, private workspace/cache layout, artifact transport, and qualification evidence at their existing boundaries. Preserve full-report plus changed-strict qualification and single-mode ordinary analysis. Replace inline-command lint assumptions with structural delegation guards and behavioral parity tests.

How to verify: Ran scripts/run_ci_quality.py --json, the complete script-test discovery, actionlint for the four analysis workflows, and git diff --check. Native Windows and unavailable external-artifact tests remain skipped. Real image qualification was not run.

Operational note: Shared verifier bytes change the noble-qt693-analysis policy identity. Fresh qualification and reviewed signed evidence are required; existing lock files were not rewritten.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Reuse validated CI object caches and retain performance evidence

Use case: Repeated application builds should reuse unchanged compiler work
without making cache persistence depend on release-upload availability.

Root cause: Linux image environment settings overrode nominal cache budgets,
Linux/macOS saved caches only after uploads, Windows had no object cache,
and accumulated cache counters obscured current-run performance.

Move verified cache saves before publication transport, enforce measured
per-lane ccache allowances through the existing launcher interface, and add
pinned Windows sccache with configuration isolation, CRT-preserving embedded
debug information and native compiler fallback. Add guarded, audit-first
closed-PR cache maintenance without deleting any remote entries.

Retain raw PR #79 evidence and add source/configuration-bound observations
and comparable cold/warm reporting. Preserve existing signed Linux environment
policy inputs byte-for-byte and document the remaining native-core blockers.

Verification: run_ci_quality.py passed all six lints and 2297 script tests
(8 skipped). Real CMake/Ninja cache and ASan/UBSan probes, six-family lock
compatibility, changed-workflow actionlint and whitespace checks passed.
Windows-native acceptance and cold plus three warm workflow runs remain
pending; no performance target or production-core reuse is claimed complete.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Preserve signed analysis policy with an ordinary CI adapter

Introduced by: 14595cf8 shared analysis execution by changing two files bound
into the published noble-qt693-analysis verification policy.
Use case: Ordinary static, coverage and CodeQL jobs must keep consuming the
existing qualified environment without fabricated replacement evidence.
Reproduction: The six-family compatibility test fails only for the analysis
family, and the real consumer rejects its current qualification-policy digest.

Restore the qualified engine and shell entry point to their approved bytes.
Route ordinary static/coverage phases through a separate adapter that imports
the unchanged engine's configuration, environment, execution, first-party
filtering and cppcheck primitives. Preserve changed-only PR scope, independent
failure propagation, coverage transport and the original-checkout ratchet.

The immutable engine has no phase API, so document partial reuse honestly and
protect remaining ordinary orchestration with command-parity tests. Production
locks, profiles, signed receipts and their verification are unchanged.

Verification: 47 qualification/adapter tests, 22 profile tests, 33 static
regressions, 16 executable namespace/failure tests and 11 focused lint tests
passed. All six production policies match again. CI lint, affected-workflow
actionlint and whitespace checks passed. The complete integrated quality gate
will run before push; remote/native analysis was not executed locally.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fix hosted CI cache activation and harden acceptance evidence

Introduced by: PR #80 cache/observation work exposed host-environment gaps;
the shell-dependent legacy logcat normalization fixture predates this PR.
Use case: Passing builds must actually exercise cache reuse, and validation
must distinguish incomplete evidence and fixture timing from correct behavior.

The first PR run inherited a real GITHUB_SHA into a synthetic observation
fixture, while native Windows uppercased VS/SDK environment names before a
case-sensitive dictionary lookup. Local fixtures did not model those inputs.
Isolate observation identities and normalize Windows lookup keys without
changing serialized identities, required fields or configuration isolation.

Restore Linux's established mtime compiler-check policy inside unchanged,
digest-qualified images. A real seeded-cache test proves that the content
policy transition alone invalidates objects; restore-only PRs could not replace
those shared seeds. Keep content checking for native macOS runner variation.

Make the legacy-error unit fixture deterministic through the existing process
seam, retain real stderr-file/notification behavior and real-child smoke, and
require observed completion with useful diagnostics. The precise old CI startup
error was not recorded; this is not claimed as a production sanitizer fix.

Reject malformed/incomplete performance evidence, exercise the consumer's real
receipt bindings, and hard-disable destructive cache cleanup until the missing
approval environment is configured and a reviewed activation removes the
interlock. Preserve the failed first PR run's actual metrics without relabeling
it as warm or successful acceptance evidence.

Verification: targeted observation, ccache, Windows cache, report, cleanup and
lock suites passed. Exact modified transport tests passed on Intel Xcode 26.6,
Qt 5.15.18 and Qt 6.9.3 with ASan+UBSan and QT_NO_KEYWORDS (44 assertions each).
Real cache invalidation and hostile Actions-environment regressions went from
RED to GREEN. Full batched quality validation will run before push; hosted
activation/warm acceptance still requires the next CI run.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>
